text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong says time to close the cracks opened in heat of recent general election, and that Singapore cannot afford a divide between English-education and Chinese-educated, or between religious groups.
- From July, ministers, judges and top civil servants to take pay cut of between 2 and 7 percent each month, in line with fall in private sector wages.
- Lion dancers and acrobats welcome President Ong Teng Cheong at the opening of Singapore River New Year event.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton calls for deeper engagement with Asia and presents centrepiece plan to strengthen American schools in annual State of Union address.

- India's Tata group chairman Ratan Tata in New Delhi with top aides in last-ditch effort to convince Indian Civil Aviation Minister to support proposed Singapore $960 million domestic airline venture with Singapore Airlines.
- Haw Par Villa theme park loses S$7.5 million in 1996, forcing owners to cut down operations and scout for a new operator.
- Creative Technology shares on rollercoaster ride over past three days.
- With little prospect G-7 finance ministers will intervene in currency markets, yen continues relentless slide.
- Singapore dollar hits three-month low against surging greenback to close at S$1.4145 to the U.S. unit.
- Pidemco Land takes up 30 percent stake in upmarket property project Canary Wharf in London.
- Philippines official corporate watchdog to investigate reports a Caucasian-run securities firm is selling bogus U.S. stocks to Singaporeans.
- Ekran Berhad gets nod to float Bakun Hydroelectric Company, owner of Bakun dam in Sarawak, in middle of this year.
- Amcol Holdings ex-partner Roland Maurel summoned to appear before Mauritius Supreme Court.
